_about: Lookup data for scripts/decode_status.py and minidump_report.py. 'class' uses the termination classes in references/universal-vocabulary.md. Verify rarely-used entries against winnt.h / ntstatus.h / signal(7) before quoting them as fact.

classes.A: Deliberate abort (fail-fast): a runtime/OS/library detected a broken invariant and ended the process on purpose. Handlers do not run.
classes.B: Hard fault: invalid memory/instruction raised by the CPU/OS (access violation, SIGSEGV, SIGBUS...).
classes.C: Unhandled language exception: a managed/C++ exception nobody caught; last-chance handlers CAN run.
classes.D: Resource exhaustion: out of memory, stack, handles.
classes.E: External kill: something else ended the process (user, script, OOM killer, supervisor, installer).
classes.F: Hang-kill: a watchdog/ANR timer ended an unresponsive process.
classes.H: Startup/loader failure: the process never really started.
classes.I: System-level: kernel panic / bugcheck / power loss took everything down.

C0000005.name: STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION
C0000005.meaning: Read/write/execute of memory that is not accessible.
C0000005.next: Params: [0]=0 read,1 write,8 DEP; [1]=address. Address < 0x10000 usually means null pointer + field offset. Find module+offset of the faulting instruction.

C000001D.name: STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION
C000001D.meaning: CPU hit an undefined instruction (corrupt code, wrong CPU features, or a deliberate trap).
C000001D.next: Check CPU/instruction-set assumptions and whether the image on disk matches the one running.

C0000006.name: STATUS_IN_PAGE_ERROR
C0000006.meaning: Could not page in a memory-mapped file (image on removed drive/network share, or failing disk).
C0000006.next: Params[2] holds the underlying NTSTATUS. Suspect running from a network/removable location.

C0000096.name: STATUS_PRIVILEGED_INSTRUCTION
C0000096.meaning: Privileged instruction in user mode (often jumped into garbage).
C0000096.next: Suspect memory corruption / bad function pointer.

C00000FD.name: STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW
C00000FD.meaning: A thread exhausted its stack (runaway recursion or huge stack allocation).
C00000FD.next: Look for a repeating module+offset pattern at the top of the faulting stack.

C0000017.name: STATUS_NO_MEMORY
C0000017.meaning: Allocation failed: out of memory/address space.
C0000017.next: Check working set / commit in heartbeat logs.

C0000374.name: STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION
C0000374.meaning: The heap manager detected corruption and fail-fasted. The bad write happened EARLIER than the crash.
C0000374.next: Do not blame the faulting frame. Use PageHeap/Application Verifier (Windows), ASan/Valgrind (Unix) to catch the original write.

C0000409.name: STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN (__fastfail)
C0000409.meaning: Despite the name this is the general __fastfail code. Params[0] is a FAST_FAIL_* reason: 2 stack-cookie check failure, 3 corrupt list entry, 5 invalid arg (CRT), 7 fatal app exit (abort()), 8 range-check failure, 10 control-flow-guard failure, 14 invalid reference count.
C0000409.next: Read Params[0] first. Verify values against winnt.h.

C0000417.name: STATUS_INVALID_CRUNTIME_PARAMETER
C0000417.meaning: C runtime invalid-parameter handler fired with no handler installed.
C0000417.next: Look for CRT calls with bad arguments near the top of the stack.

C0000420.name: STATUS_ASSERTION_FAILURE
C0000420.next: Assertion text is usually in the app log.

C0000602.name: STATUS_FAIL_FAST_EXCEPTION
C0000602.meaning: Generic fail-fast exception raised by RaiseFailFastException.
C0000602.next: The caller one or two frames above RaiseFailFastException names the subsystem that gave up.

C000027B.name: STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION
C000027B.meaning: WinRT/WinUI/COM fail-fast carrying one or more 'stowed' (saved) exceptions. Raised via RoFailFastWithErrorContext. No managed or SEH handler can intercept it.
C000027B.next: Read the stowed exception array (needs heap in dump) for the inner HRESULT and its stack. Then check WHICH THREAD fail-fasted (UI vs finalizer/worker): that distinguishes a bad call from a bad release.

80000003.name: STATUS_BREAKPOINT
80000003.meaning: int3/__debugbreak executed (assert, DebugBreak, or a deliberate runtime trap) with no debugger.
80000003.next: Look at the calling frame; usually a deliberate check.

C0000025.name: STATUS_NONCONTINUABLE_EXCEPTION
C0000025.meaning: Tried to continue after a noncontinuable exception (how RaiseFailFastException shows on stacks).
C0000025.next: Look further down the stack for the real reason.

E0434352.name: CLR managed exception (SEH wrapper)
E0434352.meaning: An unhandled .NET exception. Unlike fail-fast, AppDomain.UnhandledException runs first.
E0434352.next: Managed stack is in the Application event log (.NET Runtime, ID 1026) and in your logs.

E06D7363.name: MSVC C++ exception ('msc')
E06D7363.next: Recover the thrown type name with a debugger.

C0000135.name: STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND
C0000135.meaning: A required DLL was not found at process start.
C0000135.next: Dependency check; portable layouts and missing VC++ runtimes are common.

C0000139.name: STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND
C0000139.meaning: DLL found but lacks an expected export (version mismatch).
C0000139.next: Compare DLL versions named in the event log.

C0000142.name: STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED
C0000142.next: Check the DLL named in the Application Error event.

C000007B.name: STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_FORMAT
C000007B.meaning: Bad image: usually 32/64-bit mismatch with a dependency.
C000007B.next: Check architectures of exe and dependencies.

C000013A.name: STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT
C000013A.meaning: Console process ended by Ctrl+C / console closed.

8000000E.name: E_ILLEGAL_METHOD_CALL
8000000E.meaning: Method called in a state/time/thread where it is not allowed. In WinUI: wrong thread, object closed, or lifecycle misuse.
8000000E.next: Check which thread raised it and the object's state.

8001010E.name: RPC_E_WRONG_THREAD
8001010E.meaning: Interface was marshalled for a different thread/apartment.

80010108.name: RPC_E_DISCONNECTED
80010108.meaning: Object has disconnected from its clients.
80010108.next: Out-of-process server died or object released.

800706BA.name: RPC_S_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE
800706BA.next: Find why the server process died.

80131623.name: COR_E_FAILFAST
80131623.meaning: Commonly observed for .NET Environment.FailFast (verify on your runtime).
80131623.next: Reason string is on stderr and in the Application event log.

3.name: SIGQUIT
3.meaning: Quit with core dump (JVM: prints a thread dump instead of dying).

4.name: SIGILL
4.meaning: Illegal instruction (corrupt code, wrong CPU, or deliberate trap such as ud2).

5.name: SIGTRAP
5.meaning: Breakpoint/trap. Runtimes use it for deliberate traps (Swift/Rust on ARM; debuggers).

6.name: SIGABRT
6.meaning: abort(): the process (libc, runtime or app) deliberately gave up. glibc heap-corruption messages, assert(), Rust panic=abort, V8 fatal errors end here.

7.name: SIGBUS
7.meaning: Bad memory access (misaligned, or a mapped file was truncated). Number 7 on Linux, 10 on macOS/BSD.

9.name: SIGKILL
9.meaning: Uncatchable kill sent by someone ELSE: kill -9, OOM killer, container runtime, iOS jetsam, a supervisor. The process cannot choose it and gets no chance to log. NOT a fail-fast.

11.name: SIGSEGV
11.meaning: Invalid memory access (null/dangling pointer, stack overflow, bad write).

13.name: SIGPIPE
13.meaning: Wrote to a closed pipe/socket; default action terminates silently.

15.name: SIGTERM
15.meaning: Polite termination request (systemd stop, docker stop, kill).

31.name: SIGSYS
31.meaning: Bad system call - on Android/containers usually a seccomp policy violation.

1.meaning: Generic failure; also uncaught exception in many runtimes (Python, Node, Java main).

2.meaning: Go: panic or fatal runtime error (unrecoverable errors such as 'concurrent map writes' cannot be recover()ed).

3.meaning: MSVC CRT abort() in legacy mode.

134.meaning: Shell convention 128+6: SIGABRT (also JVM/Node fatal abort).

137.meaning: Shell convention 128+9: SIGKILL. In containers/Kubernetes very often the OOM killer.

FFFFFFFF.meaning: Windows: -1. Typical of TerminateProcess(-1) from Stop-Process -Force / taskkill /f. With no dump and no event-log crash entry this points at an EXTERNAL kill, not a crash.

-N.meaning: Python subprocess/Node child: negative returncode -N means 'killed by signal N' (-11 = SIGSEGV, -9 = SIGKILL).

EXC_BAD_ACCESS.meaning: Invalid memory access. KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS = unmapped; KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE = permissions. arm64e 'possible pointer authentication failure' = corrupted pointer.

EXC_CRASH.meaning: Process abort: uncaught Objective-C exception, abort(), assertion, or system-initiated termination (read 'Termination Reason').

EXC_BREAKPOINT.meaning: Deliberate trap: Swift runtime failures (force-unwrap nil, index out of range, failed precondition), __builtin_trap, breakpoints.

EXC_GUARD.meaning: Guarded resource misuse (e.g. closing a guarded file descriptor).

EXC_RESOURCE.meaning: Exceeded a CPU, memory, wakeups or I/O limit.

8BADF00D.meaning: 'ate bad food': watchdog killed the app for taking too long (launch/resume/scene update); main thread was blocked.

DEAD10CC.meaning: 'dead lock': app held a file lock or SQLite database while suspended in background.

DEADFA11.meaning: 'dead fall': force-quit by the user (or system unresponsive).

BAADCA11.meaning: App failed to report an incoming call to CallKit in time.
